section_summary: This section consists of diplomatic records from decimal file 894.00 covering May through August 1941, comprising the concluding appendices of the May 1941 monthly political report from Tokyo, internal State Department evaluation memoranda, and the comprehensive monthly political reports for June and July 1941 from the American Embassy in Tokyo. The reports document the deepening crisis in Japanese-American relations, driven by repeated Japanese bombings of American diplomatic and mission properties in Chungking (including the near-destruction of the USS Tutuila), missionary detentions in Korea, and the breakdown of economic negotiations with the Netherlands East Indies. They chronicle Japan's military occupation of southern French Indochina under a joint defense agreement with Vichy France, the retaliatory freezing of Japanese assets and oil export restrictions by the United States and Great Britain, the strategic shock of the German invasion of the Soviet Union, and mounting economic strain within Japan.

subfiles.about: Lists of telegrams and despatches sent to the State Department during May 1941, concluding the Tokyo Embassy's May political report.
subfiles.summary: This subfile forms the concluding portion of the Tokyo Embassy's monthly report on conditions in Japan for May 1941 (Despatch No. 5682). It provides a chronological registry of telegrams sent to the Department of State between May 14 and May 31, 1941 (Nos. 671-755), covering conversations between Ambassador Grew and Foreign Minister Matsuoka, aerial bombings of American missions in China, the Fur Seal Convention, and economic negotiations in Batavia. It also contains the complete registry of despatches forwarded in May 1941 (Nos. 5556-5630), recording detailed communications on mission property damage, commercial agreements, consular matters, and Japanese political and economic trends.
subfiles.title: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of May, 1941: Appendices (Lists of Telegrams and Despatches)

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum calling attention to the summary of Japan's economic and industrial position in the June 1941 Tokyo report.
subfiles.summary: An internal routing memorandum from the Division of Far Eastern Affairs regarding the attached political report from Tokyo for June 1941 (894.00 P.R./162). It directs the recipient to examine pages 22-23 of the report for a concise summary of Japan's economic condition. It specifically highlights the conclusion that, despite the curtailment of strategic imports from abroad, Japan had expanded its industrial capacity over the past four years and was better positioned to manufacture required goods domestically.
subfiles.title: Department of State Memorandum on Tokyo Political Report for June 1941
subfiles.to: Office of the Adviser on International Economic Affairs

subfiles.about: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew's comprehensive monthly report for June 1941 on Japanese-American friction, the German-Soviet war, and economic conditions.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmits Report No. 1676 surveying internal and foreign developments in Japan during June 1941. The report details vigorous American protests over Japanese air raids damaging the American Embassy and mission properties in Chungking, the seizure of American cargo at Haiphong, missionary detentions in Korea, and unauthorized flights over Guam. In foreign affairs, it recounts the termination of trade parleys with the Netherlands East Indies, the conclusion of a commercial treaty with Moscow followed immediately by the shocking outbreak of the German-Soviet war, and Wang Ching-wei's visit to Tokyo. Domestically, it notes the appointment of Hiroyasu Ino as Agriculture Minister, the meeting of the Central Cooperative Council of the Imperial Rule Assistance Association, commodity price pressures, acute shipping shortages, and includes complete monthly lists of June despatches (Nos. 5635-5702) and telegrams (Nos. 756-905).
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5751: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of June, 1941 (Report No. 1676)
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State, Washington

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum highlighting Ambassador Grew's warning regarding the vulnerability of Japan's economic structure under foreign trade restrictions.
subfiles.summary: An internal memorandum from the Division of Far Eastern Affairs reviewing Tokyo's Despatch No. 5812 of August 25, 1941, containing the monthly report for July 1941 (894.00 P.R./163). The memorandum notes that while most developments were previously reported by telegram, particular attention should be given to the statement on page 26. That excerpt warned that unless foreign trade restrictions against Japan are lifted, Japan's industrial, economic, and financial structure will be very substantially weakened through the loss of essential commercial relations.
subfiles.title: Department of State Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 5812, July 1941 Political Report

subfiles.about: Tokyo Embassy's monthly report for July 1941 covering Japan's military occupation of southern Indochina, U.S. asset freezing, and the near-miss bombing of the USS Tutuila.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmits Report No. 1677 documenting the grave international crisis that unfolded during July 1941. It covers Japan's military occupation of southern French Indochina under a joint defense accord with Vichy France, Ambassador Grew's conferences with new Foreign Minister Admiral Teijiro Toyoda, and the immediate American and British retaliation freezing Japanese assets and placing all commercial and oil transactions under licensing control. The report documents intense protests over repeated bombings of Chungking, culminating in a bomb detonating eight yards from the gunboat USS Tutuila on July 30, as well as embassy representations regarding missionary arrests, travel curbs, and cargo seizures. Appended to the despatch are complete monthly schedules of telegrams (Nos. 906-1141) and despatches (Nos. 5703-5762) sent in July, with the report text continuing beyond page 350.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5812: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of July, 1941 (Report No. 1677)
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State, Washington
